introSlide.title: Cybersecurity Guidelines
introSlide.subtitle: EMPLOYEE SECURITY ONBOARDING
introSlide.desc: Essential security know-how for new USC employees, aligned with Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS) baseline controls.
introSlide.desc2: Use right arrow key or space bar to advance the slides, or the on-screen 'Next' and 'Previous' buttons

module1.title: Module 1: Threats & Employee Role
module1.subtitle: MODULE 1
module1.desc: Understanding why higher education student unions are prime targets and how your daily habits protect student data.

whyMattersSlide.title: Why Cyber Security Matters Here
whyMattersSlide.card1Desc: Student Unions manage high volumes of personal records, health/dental plan sign-ups, event payments, and club financial accounts across sprawling campus networks.
whyMattersSlide.card2Desc: According to CCCS guidelines, over 85% of organization security breaches originate from social engineering or human error rather than direct system exploits.

complianceSlide.title: Canadian Compliance Frameworks
complianceSlide.r2c3: Mandatory security awareness, MFA, and access control.
complianceSlide.r3c3: Express consent & safeguards for health/dental & payment data.
complianceSlide.r4c3: Strict protection and restricted sharing of student PII.
complianceSlide.r5c3: Adherence to clean desk, safe browsing, and device policies.

hygieneSlide.title: CCCS Top Cyber Hygiene Rules
hygieneSlide.card1Desc: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on all university and staff accounts to stop unauthorized login attempts.
hygieneSlide.card2Desc: Access only the student information and financial tools required for your specific job duties (CCCS BC.12).
hygieneSlide.card3Desc: Recognize phishing tactics and report suspicious emails, links, or unknown physical visitors immediately.

module2.title: Module 2: Authentication Standards
module2.subtitle: MODULE 2
module2.desc: Implementing Canadian Centre for Cyber Security baseline recommendations for credentials and access.

mfaSlide.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Standard
mfaSlide.desc: CCCS Baseline Control BC.5 mandates MFA across all organizational systems. Password-only protection is no longer sufficient.
mfaSlide.l1Desc: Use app-based push notifications or TOTP codes (e.g., Microsoft Authenticator).
mfaSlide.l2Desc: Text messages are vulnerable to SIM swapping and interception attacks.
mfaSlide.l3Desc: Deny any unexpected MFA prompts that appear when you are not actively logging in.

passphraseSlide.title: Strong Passphrase Guidelines
passphraseSlide.l1Desc: Combine 4+ random words (e.g., maple-winter-transit-book) for 16+ characters that are easy to remember but hard to crack.
passphraseSlide.l2Desc: Never use university names, sports teams, mascot names, or your staff position in your password.
passphraseSlide.l3Desc: Store credentials in approved enterprise password vaults (e.g., 1Password, Bitwarden) rather than browser auto-fill.
passphraseSlide.l4Desc: Keep your personal campus account password completely distinct from your staff credentials.

module3.title: Module 3: Phishing & Social Engineering
module3.subtitle: MODULE 3
module3.desc: Identifying deception techniques targeted at student union executives, staff, and student volunteers.

phishingSlide.title: Spotting Phishing
phishingSlide.subtitle: Common Attack Scenarios
phishingSlide.desc1: Threat actors often impersonate Union Executives requesting urgent gift card purchases, direct deposit charges, or vendor invoice payments.
phishingSlide.desc2: Watch for spoofed university domain names (e.g., @u-canada-studentunion.ca vs official @studentunion.ca), high urgency, and unexpected attachments.

emailSlide.title: 3-Step Email Verification Process
emailSlide.card1Desc: Check sender full email header, hover over external links without clicking, and verify unexpected file attachments.
emailSlide.card2Desc: If an email requests wire transfers or payroll changes, confirm in person or call the official phone number directly.
emailSlide.card3Desc: Click the 'Report Phishing' button in Outlook/Gmail to send suspicious emails to IT for immediate review.

module4.title: Module 4: Student Data & PIPEDA Rules
module4.subtitle: MODULE 4
module4.desc: Legal standards and privacy obligations when collecting and processing student information.

privacySlide.title: Protecting Student PII & Privacy
privacySlide.subtitle: Strict Confidentiality Required
privacySlide.desc1: Student Personally Indetifiable Information (PII) - including student numbers, health plan records, financial aid claims, and event rosters - is protected under Canadian privacy laws.
privacySlide.desc2: Collect only data you strictly need, use it exclusively for approved purposes, and never share PII externally without explicit student consent.

cloudSlide.title: Safe Cloud & File Sharing Rules
cloudSlide.card1L1: Store student union documents on official tenant OneDrive or SharePoint with restricted permissions.
cloudSlide.card1L2: Share the file links with specific named accounts rather than 'Anyone with the link.'
cloudSlide.card1L3: Encrypt sensitive financial spreadsheets prior to distribution.
cloudSlide.card2L1: Transferring student records to personal Gmail, iCloud, or Dropbox accounts.
cloudSlide.card2L2: Storing unencrypted PII on unapproved personal USB drives.
cloudSlide.card2L3: Emailing unencrypted spreadsheets containing student health plan data.

module5.title: Module 5: Device & Campus Safety
module5.subtitle: MODULE 5
module5.desc: Physical security, workstation hygiene, and public campus Wi-Fi best practices.

settingsSlide.desc1: Under CCCS BC.4 (Secure Configuration), all staff hardware must maintain baseline security controls.
settingsSlide.card1Desc: Lock physical documents, keys, and access cards in drawers at the end of every shift.
settingsSlide.card2Desc: Always lock your PC (Win + L or Cmd + Ctrl + Q) when leaving your desk.
settingsSlide.card3Desc: Ensure BitLocker (Windows) or FileVault (Mac) is active on your machine.

wifiSlide.title: Campus Wi-Fi & Remote Work Safety
wifiSlide.card1Desc: Connect to encrypted campus networks (e.g., eduroam or Student Union Wi-Fi). Never perform admin duties on open public Wi-Fi without VPN.
wifiSlide.card2Desc: Use wall outlets rather than public USB charging stations to prevent 'juice jacking' malware installation.
wifiSlide.card3Desc: Use privacy screens when working in busy student hubs, cafeterias, or libraries.
wifiSlide.card4Desc: Install operating system and web browser security updates promptly when prompted.

incidentSlide.title: Incident Response & Reporting
incidentSlide.card1Desc: Disconnect Wi-Fi or network cables immediately if malware is suspected.
incidentSlide.card2Desc: Contact Union IT & Privacy Officer within 15 minutes of discovery.
incidentSlide.card3Desc: Document details, take screenshots, and do not reboot or wipe machine.
incidentSlide.card4Desc: Follow IT guidance and assist PIPEDA breach logging if required.
